feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-focused roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on outcome-based metrics beyond web scale, and could be streamlined for sharper impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines digital strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that feels current and marketable.  
- Generally clean writing with good clarity and professional tone; no obvious misspellings, and grammar is strong overall.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include impact on engagement, conversions, efficiency, revenue, campaign performance, or team productivity.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT.” These sections overlap heavily and dilute focus.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “more than 12 years experience” should be “more than 12 years’ experience” (or “12+ years of experience”); punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it with clearer positioning and one or two distinctive strengths will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your seniority and sector fit: “Digital communications and strategy leader” and mention public-sector/member or mission-driven organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with a sharper value proposition: cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, editorial systems, and analytics-informed operations.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web and CMS modernization, editorial workflow design, and digital operations that improve coordination, governance, and audience engagement. Strong background in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating complex policy or technical topics into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination also reappear in Topline Skills and Soft Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the competencies more distinct will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS management,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Replace vague items with sharper, higher-value terms: “Workflow & systems architecture” → “Digital operations & workflow architecture”; “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” → “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Prioritize the most marketable/recent strengths first: Digital strategy, web platform modernization, editorial systems, analytics, advocacy communications.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Web platform modernization & CMS management • Editorial systems & workflow design • Multi-channel communications • Analytics & performance reporting • Digital operations & systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” and “Policy & advocacy communication” repeat language already used in the header.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; consider using this section for broader themes only, leaving tools/platforms to later sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a broad responsibility list. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and distinguish it from the earlier NACo leadership role by emphasizing consulting, platform delivery, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform development, content operations, and enterprise web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one outcome-focused line: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work more concrete: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content sections, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Recast the strongest technical item as a lead achievement: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content models, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep only if tied to a new consulting outcome.
- “Analytics” and “enterprise web improvement” are vague and repeat prior experience unless quantified or linked to a specific project.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add budget size, team size, reporting cadence, production volume, efficiency gains, or engagement improvements from the studio/analytics work.
- Tighten softer phrasing: change “Strengthened digital operations…” to a result-oriented line such as “Implemented governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency, speed, and accountability.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program expansion may duplicate older roles unless framed here as building organizational production infrastructure.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned at this level.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show scope and level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around concrete ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video outcome: “Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” is very close to the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” here.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry by stressing expansion/regularization rather than initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership themes and avoid generic phrasing like “audience-focused content planning.”

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive terms:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Content governance and editorial operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Strategic content planning
- Consider “content governance and editorial operations” instead of “editorial systems and governance” for clearer leadership emphasis.
- Swap “messaging” for “communications” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- If space allows, align wording with recent work by using “enterprise web and content strategy” as the first bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems/governance” already appear in the header/Core Competencies; rephrasing helps reduce echo.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with Work Experience bullets on web, email, social, and video leadership.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize higher-value, recent strengths and group tools under impact-oriented themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not a long tool list: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal/CMS modernization first, since recent roles center on Drupal migration, microsites, and enterprise web improvement.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost exactly; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize strategic analytics leadership, not repeat the software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • Leadership reporting • User behavior analysis • SEO and performance optimization • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Put the most senior/value-add terms first; keep tools at the end as enablers.
- Replace “KPI design” with “KPI framework design” and “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting” for stronger phrasing.
- If space allows, tie to impact language used elsewhere: “decision-ready reporting” or “analytics for strategic decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current tool list duplicates the “Technical + IT” analytics section almost exactly.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language unless positioned as optimization.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with the Core Competencies line and several NACo role bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and tools/operations-focused rather than repeating broad “multimedia production.”

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize leadership and delivery scope:  
  **Multimedia Production & Event Operations**  
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event delivery  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio systems  
- Virtual event technical direction and show calling
- Replace “video production and editing” with “broadcast-quality video production and post-production” to better match the in-house studio achievement.
- Use “event operations” or “technical direction” to signal executional leadership, not just hands-on production.
- If possible, add one scale marker elsewhere on the CV (e.g., number of events, recurring series, studio built) rather than in this skills block.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media bullet about building the in-house studio.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth/relevance or removed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to show proficiency level and recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Put the most relevant platform first and consider dropping weaker/less central tools if space is tight; Drupal is clearly the anchor based on recent roles.
- If possible, add a qualifier in the section heading or line, e.g. “CMS Platforms” or “CMS Platforms (enterprise + team publishing)” to make it more meaningful.
- Keep formatting parallel and concise; avoid a simple undifferentiated tool dump.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical context.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight beside enterprise CMS tools unless supported elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current, implementation-focused, and specific to tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied delivery: “Front-End & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Deployment.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add scope/level instead of just tools: “Front-end implementation, API integrations, tag management, edge scripting, CI/CD automation.”
- Consider replacing older/less strategic items with stronger recent signals if true (e.g., “Drupal theming,” “GA4/measurement implementation,” “AI search integration”) to better match 2022–present work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless you specifically want this section purely implementation-oriented.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Rename to emphasize systems ownership, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Tighten and group by function: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Prioritize tools most aligned with recent work and leadership scope; keep Airtable, Power Automate, Jira/Asana, Slack/Teams, and consider dropping Basecamp or Trello if less current.
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: “Built and managed workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate; coordinated delivery in Jira/Asana; supported cross-team operations in Slack and Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar PM tools—listing all four may feel padded unless all are genuinely current.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one functional qualifier to increase relevance without duplicating experience bullets, e.g.: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys (campaign automation)** • **Higher Logic (member communications)** • **Mailchimp**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one is older/light exposure, consider removing it to strengthen credibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding phrases like “newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “email strategy” here; those are already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies.
- If Higher Logic was your primary NACo platform, consider whether listing both Higher Logic and Mailchimp overstates overlap unless both were materially used.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to “firsts” or scale achieved during this earlier period.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational impact: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped standardize day-to-day digital production workflows.”
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social output, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or early production rather than expansion.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” is similar to later governance/operations bullets; keep this version tactical, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, cross-functional support, and the podcast as the clearest distinctive outcome.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, and launched the organization’s first podcast.”
- Add scope/action detail without overclaiming: “Managed podcast planning, scripting, guest coordination, and production; also supported digital and multimedia content for program communications.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to” and “materials” with stronger verbs: supported, produced, coordinated, developed.
- If available, add one measurable outcome: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video or digital leadership here; save that progression for 2015–2024 roles.
